title: A Country Herbal for the Glen
author: Hester Lowe, midwife
notes: Extra shelf book: bellwort root and dried nightshade are real items in the game; the bell line is folk memory (bell source, lightly).

pages.text:
Bellwort. A pale, nodding flower, the root bitter and steadying. Grows thickest along the priory road, where old women say the bell was once heard clearest. Chewed, it settles a racing heart and a restless night.

Nightshade. Dried, a drop of the tincture will let a person sleep who has not slept in a week. Too much and they will not wake. I have been asked to make it stronger. I have not.

For a child who will not sleep: warm milk, a little honey, a cloth over the window, and a song. Any song. Not the one from the hill.
